candidates.title: Ryanair passenger describes 'traumatic' Murcia flight bomb threat
candidates.summary: Sarah Jones says passengers had to wait in a hangar for three hours after landing at Murcia in Spain
candidates.reason: Dedupe: live item has no exact/history repeat; accepted for editorial selection. | Selection: Protected item selected before size limits.
candidates.practical_angle: Есть новый городской контекст для Greater Manchester.
candidates.lead: Sarah Jones says passengers had to wait in a hangar for three hours after landing at Murcia in Spain
candidates.evidence_text: Ryanair passenger describes 'traumatic' Murcia flight bomb threat - BBC News Image source, Sarah Jones Image caption, Charlotte (left), Sarah and Kelly travelled to Spain to work as medics at a golf tournament By Haider Saleem North West Published 3 November 2026 The evacuation of a Ryanair aircraft after a suspected bomb threat has been described as "quite traumatic" by a passenger who was on board the flight. Sarah Jones said police, fire crews and bomb disposal officers surrounded the plane after it landed at Murcia airport from Manchester. The medic from Manchester said she and her fellow passengers were told to leave their belongings on board and then spent about three hours in an airport hangar while the plane was searched. Spanish officials said no explosives were found. The aircraft was one of seven searched at airports across Europe following a series of suspected bomb threats. Image source, Sarah Jones Image caption, Emergency services attended Murcia airport after the Ryanair aircraft landed Jones was travelling with colleagues Charlotte and Kelly to work as medics at a golf tournament in La Manga in south-eastern Spain. She said the flight was uneventful until the aircraft landed at about 10:30 local time (09:30 GMT). "When we landed, the plane just sort of stopped really quickly and we were held there for a while," she told the BBC. Passengers initially thought they were waiting for permission to taxi to the terminal. "Then we were just surrounded by police, the bomb squad, ambulances were there, fire engines," she said. "Then we were told that we needed to evacuate the plane, but we weren't allowed to bring anything off. "We had to leave the luggage in the overhead lockers." Image source, Sarah Jones Image caption, Passengers walked away from the aircraft after being told to leave their belongings on board Jones said passengers walked towards the airport and were initially given little information about what had happened. She said a police officer told her there had been a security threat, but would not confirm whether it involved the airport or the plane. They were later told there had been a bomb threat made against their aircraft, Jones said. She said sniffer dogs searched the plane and passengers' luggage was checked. "I think we were more frustrated that we didn't know what was going on," she said. Image caption, Airports in Spain, Italy, Poland and Bulgaria where planes were searched following suspected bomb threats Jones said passengers remained calm but spent time outside in hot weather before being offered water. They were eventually allowed to return to the plane through its rear door to collect their luggage, before leaving through the front door and going through the airport. Jones said they did not leave the airport until after 14:00 local time. Spanish officials said 121 people, including crew, had been on board the flight. Other aircraft were inspected in Poland, Italy and Bulgaria. It is not known whether the threats were connected. The UK government described the incidents as "malicious hoax threats" and said it had well-tested procedures for handling potential aviation threats. The aircraft was one of seven searched at airports across Europe following a series of suspected bomb threats Jones was travelling with colleagues Charlotte and Kelly to work as medics at a golf tournament in La Manga in south-eastern Spain She said the flight was uneventful until the aircraft landed at about 10:30 local time (09:30 GMT)

candidates.evidence_text: A fleet of weed harvesters are helping to clean up the waterways in north-west England The Canal & River Trust is spending more than £150,000 to use machines called Truxors to remove aquatic weeds like duckweed, floating pennywort and azolla, which when left unchecked can cause problems for boats The weeds can also starve underwater plants of light and reduce levels of oxygen needed by fish and other wildlife, and can have a damaging impact on kingfishers and otters Kieran Howlett, from the Canal & River Trust, said managing the weeds was becoming more challenging but the charity was determined to protect the "wonderful waterways" With warmer summers and longer growing seasons, these fast-growing plants spread quickly through the canal network and can rapidly form a thick green carpet across the water's surface Described as "a bit like floating tractors" by the Canal & River Trust, the specialist machines cut and collect weeds from the water, helping the team remove about 30 tonnes each week

The blaze broke out at a 'commercial building' on Bell Street at around 2.20pm on Monday (November 2). Fire crews, police officers and paramedics were called to the street At the height of the large blaze , six fire engines and two aerial ladder platforms were used to tackle the flames. Sadly, the man was pronounced dead at the scene of the fire His next of kin has been informed. candidates.evidence_text: Bolton New cenotaph approved to remember 155 heroes from three Bolton villages The decision has been hailed as a ‘historic moment’ for the area after a four-year campaign Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 06:46, Plans have been approved for a new cenotaph to commemorate the fallen of three villages on the outskirts of Bolton . The 12ft high memorial structure now has permission to be built in the grounds of St Saviour church, Fold Road, Stoneclough Applicant David De Souza said the cenotaph would commemorate the sacrifices of service people from Stoneclough, Ringley and Prestolee He said Bolton council’s planning approval represented ‘a historic moment’ for the area after a four-year campaign to reach this stage The structure’s designs state it will be made from sandstone, which would be sympathetic to churchyard and conservation area and its sculptural elements would include two 5 ft 8 in soldiers, standing reversed arms It will have an 8×8 foot paved base with no steps required to approach it

Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter Transport bosses in Greater Manchester say there are no plans for a congestion charge in the city centre amid concerns traffic levels across the region are getting out of hand A report published by Manchester council on Tuesday (November 3) revealed traffic has become so bad that it is sucking billions of pounds out of the region’s economy - on top of causing issues with delays and air quality Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) said it will ‘invest heavily’ in public transport to try and turn the situation around, with £2.5bn of government money set to flow into the region between 2027 and 2032, and plans to bring railway lines into the Bee Network starting from t A spokesperson added: “There are no plans for a congestion charge in any part of Greater Manchester, instead we are investing heavily in the Bee Network to give people a reliable alternative to getting in their car “One tram full of people could replace around 200 cars on the road and a double decker bus around 75, demonstrating the benefits of getting more people on board the Bee Network.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Transport for Greater Manchester Greater Manchester's £1 billion congestion problem Traffic levels on Greater Manchester's roads are getting worse, according to a new report. Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter Transport bosses in Greater Manchester say there are no plans for a congestion charge in the city centre amid concerns traffic levels across the region are getting out of hand A report published by Manchester council on Tuesday (November 3) revealed traffic has become so bad that it is sucking billions of pounds out of the region’s economy - on top of causing issues with delays and air quality Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) said it will ‘invest heavily’ in public transport to try and turn the situation around, with £2.5bn of government money set to flow into the region between 2027 and 2032, and plans to bring railway lines into the Bee Network starting from t A spokesperson added: “There are no plans for a congestion charge in any part of Greater Manchester, instead we are investing heavily in the Bee Network to give people a reliable alternative to getting in their car “One tram full of people could replace around 200 cars on the road and a double decker bus around 75, demonstrating the benefits of getting more people on board the Bee Network.”

Dawid Bialek, 30, sold heroin and crack-cocaine to vulnerable users, police said Footage from seized mobile phones uncovered as part of an ongoing investigation after his initial arrest captured him pretending to be a fast-food server, GMP added. The footage has now been released as he begins a jail term The video features a man's voice saying to a user through an open window: "Hello can I take your order please? What would you like?" "Your order is on its way sir," adds the voice. "Order number 6829, ready for collection." The footage shows cash on a sofa as small packages of drugs are counted out. The term 'eight white' can be heard before the voice says: "That's our little McDonald's game, that's what we're playing." Police said wraps of crack-cocaine and heroin were being prepared in the footage

Several fire crews attended and fought the blaze for more two hours Images at the time showed thick plumes of smoke could be seen from many areas of the town In the past week, a planning application has been filed with Wigan council to build a taller building at the site, following its destruction. Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter Transport bosses in Greater Manchester say there are no plans for a congestion charge in the city centre amid concerns traffic levels across the region are getting out of hand A report published by Manchester council on Tuesday (November 3) revealed traffic has become so bad that it is sucking billions of pounds out of the region’s economy - on top of causing issues with delays and air quality Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) said it will ‘invest heavily’ in public transport to try and turn the situation around, with £2.5bn of government money set to flow into the region between 2027 and 2032, and plans to bring railway lines into the Bee Network starting from t A spokesperson added: “There are no plans for a congestion charge in any part of Greater Manchester, instead we are investing heavily in the Bee Network to give people a reliable alternative to getting in their car “One tram full of people could replace around 200 cars on the road and a double decker bus around 75, demonstrating the benefits of getting more people on board the Bee Network.”

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton New cenotaph approved to remember 155 heroes from three Bolton villages The decision has been hailed as a ‘historic moment’ for the area after a four-year campaign Add to preferred sources Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 06:46, Plans have been approved for a new cenotaph to commemorate the fallen of three villages on the outskirts of Bolton . The 12ft high memorial structure now has permission to be built in the grounds of St Saviour church, Fold Road, Stoneclough Applicant David De Souza said the cenotaph would commemorate the sacrifices of service people from Stoneclough, Ringley and Prestolee He said Bolton council’s planning approval represented ‘a historic moment’ for the area after a four-year campaign to reach this stage The structure’s designs state it will be made from sandstone, which would be sympathetic to churchyard and conservation area and its sculptural elements would include two 5 ft 8 in soldiers, standing reversed arms It will have an 8×8 foot paved base with no steps required to approach it

The Manchester Evening News and other media organisations are not naming the man in order to protect his victim's anonymity. He later researched online articles on date rape drugs; sleeping tablets; and the interaction of medication and alcohol, jurors were told

His loved ones raised the alarm after his messages home stopped An appeal to find him was launched. Communities at 14 places across the borough will join the country in a two-minute silence to remember those involved in the two world wars and later conflicts Leader of Wigan Council, Coun Nazia Rehman, said: “Remembrance Sunday brings us together as a country and as a borough, commemorating those who have served and sacrificed as part of our Armed Forces “It is a deeply solemn occasion, a moment to reflect as a community on the duty, honour, bravery and selflessness of our armed forces and their families, across Britain and the Commonwealth, and to remember those lost to conflict or terrorism.” “There are parades and services taking place across our borough and everyone is welcome to attend and be part of this meaningful day.” There has been a small change of route for the Wigan parade, and in Leigh the parade will form on St Mary’s Way instead of Railway Road

Communities at 14 places across the borough will join the country in a two-minute silence to remember those involved in the two world wars and later conflicts Leader of Wigan Council, Coun Nazia Rehman, said: “Remembrance Sunday brings us together as a country and as a borough, commemorating those who have served and sacrificed as part of our Armed Forces “It is a deeply solemn occasion, a moment to reflect as a community on the duty, honour, bravery and selflessness of our armed forces and their families, across Britain and the Commonwealth, and to remember those lost to conflict or terrorism.” “There are parades and services taking place across our borough and everyone is welcome to attend and be part of this meaningful day.” There has been a small change of route for the Wigan parade, and in Leigh the parade will form on St Mary’s Way instead of Railway Road

candidates.evidence_text: Didsbury Didsbury bar vows 'fresh start' after 20-year restriction is lifted The Didsbury bar was at a Manchester council licensing hearing on Monday Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 12:28, 03 Nov 2026 View A bar in Didsbury has promised a ‘fresh start’ after it managed to remove a licensing restriction on music which had been in place for 20 years The Drawing Room on Burton Road appeared at a Manchester council licensing hearing on Monday (November 2) after applying to remove the 20-year-old condition that any music played must be ‘purely incidental’ It said it had been advised to apply to remove the decades-old condition because it was ‘not considered relevant’ to its current operations But the venue faced an initial objection from Manchester council’s licensing and out of hours team , as well as letters from councillors raising concerns about the impact of the bar on the local community Abi Pulleyn, owner of the Drawing Room, said she would bring in new measures to turn the situation around

Burba, 31, was four times above the legal drug-drive limit when he had an epileptic fit at the wheel and smashed his wife's Peugeot van into a tree between junctions 34 and 33 of the motorway ne Ryan, who was in the front passenger seat, died 'in terror' as he tried to gain control of the vehicle moments before the crash on April 20 last year. Weeks before, Burba, formerly of Arnside Crescent, Morecambe, had been warned not to drive due to his medical condition He had previously been told by his doctor in October 2014 to stop taking cocaine after he suffered a seizure which lasted up to four minutes. He was given a similar warning in February when he was admitted to hospital after more fits, and was also told to inform the DVLA of his e In August 2025, he was jailed for 10 years after pleading guilty to causing death by dangerous driving. He also admitted driving without a licence and with no insurance

candidates.evidence_text: Harpurhey Harpurhey by-election candidate issues statement after he's slammed for 'illegal' M62 photos Labour's candidate in the Harpurhey by-election has apologised and deleted the images Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Demo Labour’s candidate in the Harpurhey by-election has apologised and deleted images after rivals accused him of 'feeling he was above the law'. Abdul Sarfraz is standing for the vacant seat at Manchester City Council in a by-election which is taking place on November 26 Images shared on Sarfraz’s X account in 2024 and 2025, seen by the Manchester Evening News , showed pictures taken from the driver’s seat of a car. One image from July 2025 appears to be taken from inside a Range Rover moving slowly on the M62 A second picture from June 2024 showed the Labour candidate using his phone while behind the wheel in heavy traffic. The images were deleted after the MEN approached Labour for comment Mr Sarfraz said he was ‘genuinely sorry’ for the ‘inappropriate’ behaviour. His rivals accused him of showing ‘complete disregard’ for road safety The Reform UK group on Manchester council said: “Abdul Sarfraz, the Manchester Labour candidate for the Harpurhey by-election, clearly feels he is above the law, a charge voters increasingly level at politicians these days

candidates.evidence_text: Andy Burnham 'Manchesterism' shortlisted for UK's Word of the Year for 2026 thanks to Andy Burnham It wasn't enough to claim the top crown though Add to preferred sources Comments News Adam Maidment What's On and LGBTQ+ Writer 09:39, 03 Nov 2026 View The term ‘Manchesterism’ has been shortlisted for Word of the Year, after the Prime Minister brought the term back into popular use Whilst it was ‘Mogging’, a word meaning to outperform or dominate someone, earned the top title of the Collins Word of the Year 2026, the likes of ‘carspreading’ and ‘hydration break’, notably used during the 2026 FIFA World Cup , were also up for contention For ‘Manchesterism’, the 19th-century term, which originally described the economic movement and argued that markets should be free from government regulation and tariffs, was brought back into popular use this year thanks to Prime Minister Andy Burnham During his election campaign, the Prime Minister, who is the former Mayor for Greater Manchester, used the term to describe a political vision focused on public transport integration and localised decision making across the country "Manchesterism is a modern and functional response to the high-inequality, low-growth trap that came from the 1980s drive to over-centralise political power in the Treasury and privatise economic power," Mr Burnham said back in May

"He was really vulnerable and a lot more when he was under the influence."

candidates.evidence_text: Andy Burnham Downing Street speaks out on £20,000 claim after plane stops at Manchester Airport for Andy Burnham and his wife The Prime Minister was collected at Manchester Airport with his wife Marie-France van Heel, 34 minutes after taking off from Downing Street has said it will 'not comment on speculative figures' after a flight to Manchester to pick up Andy Burnham was reported to have cost £20,000 The flight took off from London Stansted at around 6am on Monday morning (November 2) for Antigua and Barbuda ahead of the Commonwealth leaders’ summit - but the Prime Minister was not on board with UK delegates. Mr Burnham was then collected at Manchester along with his wife, Ma Former prime minister Gordon Brown was also on the Government plane. The Guido Fawkes website estimated the cost of the Stansted-Manchester flight as £20,000 But the Prime Minister's spokesperson defended the decision and said security, operational reasons and value for money for the taxpayer were all considerations when deciding on how the Prime Minster travels. The spokesperson said: “The Prime Minister’s travel arrangements are mad "The Prime Minister’s travel arrangements reflect where he was carrying out official government business at the end of last week. He spent the day in Scotland on Friday, returned to Manchester to work from Number 10 North on Friday evening.”

Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

Credit: UK Parliament A Labour MP has revealed that she is a victim of domestic abuse - Speaking in the Commons on October 13, Kirith Entwistle, who represents Bolton North East, described her experience of the current court system as "triggering", adding that she had to watch her abuser "stare at her" during a recent video hearing Ms Entwistle told her fellow MPs that she believes special measures - where victims are given protection or assistance in court - should be the standard in cases involving domestic abuse Examples of these measures could include screens, the ability to give evidence through a live link, or witnesses being able to be accompanied when giving evidence Measures to protect victims are included in the Courts and Tribunals Bill, which is currently going through Parliament Speaking during a debate on the bill, Ms Entwistle said: "It doesn’t matter how many times somebody tells me that they understand what I’m going through, or they acknowledge what I’ve been through, they really don’t unless they have lived it themselves or know somebody who has."

Credit: 499883 A man who murdered a mother and four of her children in a firebomb attack had been arrested and released by police despite Zak Bolland, 26, walked free from a police station after giving a 12-minute ‘no comment’ interview for breaking the windows of the home of Michelle Pearson, 37, and her young family in Jackson Street in Walkden, Greater Manchester on November 26 2017 Bolland’s previous convictions and suspended jail sentence he was serving at the time had not been checked by police and he was told he would be ‘NFA’d’ – no further action taken against him over the windows attack, Bolton Coroner’s Court heard Thirteen days later, in the dead of night on December 11 2017, he smashed Ms Pearson’s windows again and tossed in a petrol bomb which “exploded” near the stairs, blocking the only exit to the ground floor and trapping the victims upstairs Demi Pearson, 15, her brother Brandon, eight, and sisters Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, all died in the blaze Ms Pearson suffered 68% burns to her body and “clung on to life” until she died, 20 months after the attack on August 25 2019

english_fact_card.what_happened: Developer Zentra has submitted revised plans to Manchester City Council for a six-storey apartment building off Old Mill Street and Lampwick Lane. The scheme, originally approved for 40 flats and commercial units, is now proposed as fully affordable housing with 41 apartments (19 one-bed, 20 two-bed, 1 three-bed, 1 four-bed) and no commercial space. L&Q is in talks to acquire the completed scheme for social rent.

candidates.evidence_text: An 'unparalleled' investigation shows a third of staff surveyed have experienced bad behaviour from senior officials A scathing report into Manchester City Council's working culture has found a prevailing “boys' club” mentality and widespread bad behaviour by senior staff. The internal document – that will be shared with council workers tomorrow and is based on a survey of nearly 1,200 staff – The report describes a culture at the council in which senior staff can act inappropriately with seeming impunity. Many junior staff members believe raising issues will lead to retaliation, and 59% of survey respondents have witnessed or experienced a form of harassment, discrimi One worker recalled a young apprentice being repeatedly sexually harassed by a senior colleague until she was forced to leave the council. “He was allowed to stay,” they said of the offending staffer. “She was interviewed by two male managers and needless to say she left.” There A council worker, speaking to us on the condition of anonymity, said of the report: “if I were a manager that would sicken me to my core.” When we approached the council before publishing this story, CEO Tom Stannard said: “it is completely unacceptable that anyone should feel undervalued, unable to raise concerns, unsupported if they do or – in the worst cases – unsafe. These issues cannot and will not be ignored.”

candidates.evidence_text: From the fabulous Feast of Fire celebrations to the iconic Christmas Lights Switch-On, the town centre will host an exciting calendar of entertainment as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture 2026 The programme will showcase the very best of Oldham's culture, creativity and community spirit with a series of free family-friendly events The programme begins with the Feast of Fire event on Saturday 31 October 2026. A joint celebration of Halloween and Bonfire Night, this spellbinding event will light up the heart of the town centre with fire dance performances and The Lips Halloween Show by Puppets with Guts foll Then, just two weeks later, the festive season will officially begin with the Oldham Christmas Lights Switch-On event on Saturday 14 November, starting from 1pm. The day will feature meet and greets with Peppa Pig, appearances from Oldham's mascots and activities by the Spindles The celebrations will continue into the evening with the big Switch On Show from 5.30pm featuring Father Christmas, Peppa Pig's Dance Party, Oldham Rock Choir and performances from Fierce Dance The Mayor of Oldham Cllr Pam Byrne will also take part in the celebrations before a local school child competition winner will switch on the town's Christmas lights. The evening will conclude with a festive fireworks finale, accompanied by a lights and laser show

candidates.evidence_text: The borough of Rochdale blossomed with success at this year’s North West in Bloom awards, celebrating a bumper year achieving 21 gold awards and 8 overall category wins The outstanding results were announced at the annual awards ceremony at the Toughsheet Community Stadium in Bolton on Thursday, 30 October 2026, following Royal Horticultural Society (RHS) judges visiting in the summer. The awards recognise the borough’s success in horticulture, Following the outstanding gold achievement and scooping the overall Town Centres and City Centres title at the recent Royal Horticultural Society Britain in Bloom awards, Rochdale town centre’s horticulturists remained on their winning streak taking gold and best in category for Rochdale in Bloom treasurer Phil Massey also received an outstanding contribution award for his significant work supporting Rochdale’s success in both national and local efforts Baillie Street Quarter won the new Best Art in the Community award for outstanding artwork from the recent Common Walls International Mural Festival, organised by talented local artist Hayley Garner (Ayo). Rochdale BID also secured gold and won the Best Business Improvement Distr Hampton by Hilton hotel entered for the first time this year, taking gold and category winner, alongside a gold for nearby Norton Grange hotel in the Large Accommodation category

Download Judging is now under way for the inaugural Bury Education Awards, launched by Bury Council in partnership with the Bury Times to celebrate the outstanding contribution of schools, educational settings, staff, governors and young people across the borough The awards recognise excellence across 11 categories The Jennifer Lowe Early Years Provider of the Year Award has been named in recognition of Jennifer's contribution to early years education in Bury, ensuring her legacy continues through the celebration of excellence in the sector. candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. The city comes alive with a plethora of family-friendly activities, ensuring that children of all ages have a memorable and joyful experience. candidates.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. Born in London into a Gambian griot lineage of seven centuries, she began learning the kora at age three with her brother Tunde Jegede and father Sanjally Jobarteh; her cousin was the late Toumani Diabaté. She studied at the Royal College of Music, the Purcell School of Music and SOAS University of London. In 2015 she founded The Gambia Academy, which puts African history and culture at the centre of its curriculum, and she has keynoted forums hosted by the UN and the World Trade Organization. In 2023 Berklee College of Music awarded her an honorary Doctorate in Music alongside Usher and Roberta Flack

candidates.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

candidates.evidence_text: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument. candidates.lead: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867.
candidates.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

candidates.evidence_text: The event will bring together more than 20 venues for cocktail takeovers, tastings, collaborations and special events Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Manchester is getting a brand new dedicated cocktail festival this November, with a week-long programme of events taking place across some of the city’s best-known bars Manchester Cocktail Festival will run from Monday 9 to Sunday 15 November, bringing together more than 20 venues for guest bartender appearances, special cocktail menus, tastings, dining experiences and industry events The festival has been created by Nick Coupland of Liar’s Group, the hospitality company behind Crazy Pedro’s, Cane & Grain and Science + Industry, alongside Ben Kendrick of Speak In Code and Double Down Inspired by similar festivals in other UK cities, the pair hope to celebrate Manchester’s cocktail scene while creating opportunities for collaboration between bars, drinks brands and hospitality professionals Participating venues include Speak In Code, Blinker, The Morris, Winsome, Bar Shrimp, Double Down, Stray, Bar Dos, Crazy Pedro’s and Hawksmoor, alongside Northern Quarter favourites Science + Industry, The Daisy and The Bay Horse Tavern

The opening marks Open Restaurant Group’s 9th restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Di At the heart of the restaurant will be a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, placing guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot; th From the grill, guests can expect the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallo t, alongside Turbot Steak, a bone-in cut finished with brown butter, green chilli and preserved lemon

Some things needed revisiting and tidying u Alastair stressed product discipline in order to understand the business driver and the outcome you want. At Peninsula, one initiative focused on giving customers richer answers and delivered over £1m in revenue. He said success depends on strong sponsorship and expertise from wi Tripti described spending three years building data foundations at Kellanova, focusing on "the right things at the right time" and bringing business teams along on the journey. They started with UK field sales as a proof of concept initially

candidates.lead: JD Sports has come a long way from its roots as a single shop in the Greater Manchester town of Bury.
candidates.evidence_text: The AI agents transforming £13bn JD Sports Posted on November 3, 2026 by Jonathan Symcox The AI agents transforming £13bn JD Sports Matt Lemon, head of supply chain technology, explains at Manhattan Exchange conference how agentic AI is ‘unpicking legacy constraints’ Share: Listen to article Retail JD Sports has come a long way from its roots as a single shop in the Greater Manchester town of Bury. Forty-five years on, JD Group is a £13 billion revenue global retailer of sports, fashion and outdoor brands. Having made more than a dozen major acquisitions over the years, it now has more than 4,800 stores across 51 countries, alongside multiple online channels. After embracing AI platforms to connect more potential customers with its products, it is also looking to harness the emerging technology to improve processes – including in its supply chain. Matt Lemon, JD’s head of supply chain technology, has this year taken part in an agentic AI pilot programme run by unified commerce and supply chain software company Manhattan Associates alongside the likes of L’Oréal. Lemon took part in a panel discussion at the recent Manhattan Exchange conference in Milan alongside Raphaël Herve, senior director – technical & support services at Manhattan Associates; CEVA Logistics IT director Johan Berghs; and Antoine Prat, fulfillment process global director at L’Oréal. He explained to BusinessCloud afterwards how agentic AI is ‘unpicking legacy constraints’. “What we’re doing is lifting away from the legacy systems that we’ve inherited over the years, either through acquisition or through development of our own business at speed,” he says. “When you see the rapid growth of JD over the past 15-20 years, we’ve not really had that opportunity to just stop and assess, then rebuild for the correct technological future. “So a lot of the work that I’ve been trying to do in my four years with JD is to unpick some of the legacy constraints we have – and tools like agentic AI really help me to do that.” One example of an operational AI agent deployed by JD is a ‘wave coordinator’ which manages and schedules the release of order batches – called ‘waves’ – to the warehouse floor. “The wave coordinator is there to effectively analyse our workload, our order profile, and then create the wave strategies to optimise the flow through the warehouse,” explains Lemon. “Thinking of it from the point of view of a control room manager, we ask: what would I need to make my processes faster? And for me, it’s to remove that decision-making which could take multiple hours [for a human to perform]. “How do we sequence our distribution across Europe: to France, to Spain, to Italy, to Sweden, to wherever we want to ship to? Let’s just not think about it anymore – let’s have an agent do that for us. “We’ve seen a really strong use case in that area in the past few weeks.” Tesco eyes 150 Poundland stores amid administration Manhattan Associates CEO Eric Clark told its 10th annual EMEA customer and partner gathering that “complexity in your software is a tax”. His chosen metaphor was an airliner cockpit which once upon a time required five crew, but now needs two as the instruments absorb that complexity. In AI-enabled warehouse terms, its software now claims to make deployments up to 50% faster, while stores and orders can go live in as little as 100 days – a rapid improvement on a year ago. Lemon says one of the major operational benefits of its AI agents is “getting back time to make decisions elsewhere”. “The tech-focused agents are allowing us to free up the real skilled people that understand our business and core systems to focus on something else – instead of responding to a data issue on the end of a ticket or a routine and repetitive incident that arises in a facility,” he continues. “So what we’re really doing is just shifting the focus of people – that’s where we’re finding the value.” Related Stories View All Tesco eyes 150 Poundland stores amid administration Protein Works CEO named Business Woman of the Year THG plc shares rocket on trading update Wayfair fined £4.8m by UK competitions watchdog Insights View All Related Stories View All Tesco eyes 150 Poundland stores amid administration Protein Works CEO named Business Woman of the Year THG plc shares rocket on trading update Wayfair fined £4.8m by UK competitions watchdog Insights View All Subscribe to our newsletter This site is protected by reCAPTCHA and the Google Privacy Policy and Terms of Servi

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Art Fair has announced details of a prestigious three-night chef residency ahead of its much-anticipated return to the city later this month Combining the worlds of contemporary art and fine dining, the fair, which runs from Thu 19 Nov – Sun 22 Nov , will host Cumbria’s Michelin-starred The Forest Side and Head Chef Paul Leonard In what will be the restaurant’s first Manchester residency, Leonard will create bespoke dining experiences for leading art buyers, collectors and VIP guests at Manchester Central. The partnership is a significant expansion of last year’s collaboration, which saw Leonard and Manc At The Forest Side in Grasmere, Leonard is renowned for his creative, ingredient-led approach to modern British cuisine, drawing inspiration from the Cumbrian landscape and its seasonal produce, including ingredients grown and foraged from the restaurant’s 45-acre grounds Under his leadership, the restaurant has retained its Michelin Star, first awarded in 2016, and was awarded a Michelin Green Star earlier this year in recognition of its commitment to sustainability and ingredient provenance. The hotel also received a Michelin Key in 2024 The initiative has been championed by Manchester Art Fair Executive Chair Thom Hetherington, who was previously involved in the launch of Restaurant magazine and The World’s 50 Best Restaurants Awards

This is all accompanied by Yorkshire puddings, roast potatoes, seasonal veg and Zouk’s signature spicy g For those who prefer a Christmas curry, there are aromatic dishes including Turkey Tikka Masala, Lamb Rogan Josh and Goan Fish Curry. Poppadoms and pickles, starters and festive desserts, including a Snowberry Pavlova, complete the festive feast Alongside the magic emanating from the kitchen, Zouk will be transformed into an elegant winter wonderland, and dinnertime entertainment will be supplied by a Christmas magician between 1pm – 5pm Zouk’s five-course Christmas Day banquet is priced at £79.95 per person, with a dedicated vegetarian and vegan banquet available for £55 per person. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

candidates.evidence_text: Lowry , Salford 4 November 2026 Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit Few songs are quite as instantly associated with Greater Manchester as Brian and Michael’s 1978 hit ‘Matchstalk Men and Matchstalk Cats and Dogs’. Written about the life and paintings of L. S. Lowry, it turned one of the region’s best-known artists into an unlikely pop culture ph Coming to Lowry this November, Matchstalks Remastered is a playful music-theatre performance inspired by the song, the artist and the city that connects them. Two performers, accompanied by live jazz musician Adam Fairhall and a record player, attempt to follow a constantly scrol As the record plays, movement, storytelling and slapstick collide. Kevin Egan and Michael Pinchbeck shift between performers, songwriters, Lowry himself and the familiar figures populating his paintings, using the structure of the original song to create a series of theatrical sc Along the way, the production follows Lowry’s footsteps around Manchester and plays with the way stories about artists are remembered and retold. How does a painting become a song? What happens when that song becomes theatre? And what gets lost, exaggerated or reinvented along th The performance also arrives in the year marking the 50th anniversary of Lowry’s death, offering an appropriately unconventional way to revisit an artist whose industrial landscapes remain closely tied to the identity of Greater Manchester

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. candidates.evidence_text: Дронотур Бумбокса Європою. Листопад-грудень 2026 року. Презентація максі-синглу "Живий" Кожного разу, коли перед менеджментом гурту Бумбокс стоїть завдання написати пресреліз, ми починаємо згадувати цікаві факти. Скільки концертів зіграли, скільки грошей зібрали, які пісні видали. Це база. Непогано ще пам’ятати, чи був гурт у країні, до якої ми збираємося, чи це пер О, як би хотілося написати: "Концерт гурту Бумбокс" — і як у Львові за добу продано 8000 квитків. Так-так, ми не про Львів розповідаємо, хоча теж про Європу Наші віддані слухачі, якщо ви перебуваєте за кордоном, сподіваємось, вам буде цікаво дізнатися, що після традиційної перерви на декілька місяців, Бумбокс поїде в турне від Ізраїлю до Німеччини, від Англії до Польщі, від Ірландії до Словаччини та Чехії І повеземо ми в це турне свіженький, як херсонський кавун, максі-сингл “Живий”, підсилений піснями з різних альбомів, під частину яких виросли ви, а під частину зростають ваші діти Тож ознайомтеся, будь ласка, уважно з розкладом туру, купуйте квитки заздалегідь, готуйте гроші на донати та мерч — зустрінемося в листопаді

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events International Trade Forum - November International Trade Forum - November Official Chamber Post FREE Manchester Hall, 36 Bridge Street Manchester, M3 3BT Wednesday 4 Nov 10am - 12pm Sponsored By Monex Book Now Join Greater Manchester Chamber’s International Trade Forum, br Attendees will have the opportunity to hear from expert speakers, take part in discussions on key trade themes and connect with fellow businesses involved in international markets November's Trade Forum will be sponsored by Monex , our Strategic Partners, supporting members across all their currency and foreign exchange requirements. They'll be diving into the UK Budget and giving a 2027 Economic and Currency Market Outlook. Our Partner experts will be on Monex is a global financial services group with more than 40 years of experience helping businesses navigate global markets through foreign exchange expertise, market insights, and risk management solutions. Through its top-ranked research team, Monex is regularly recognised amon Representing Monex at this year's Forum will be Dr. Nick Rees , Head of Macro Research at Monex, alongside Katie Bragol i, Head of Corporate Sales, and Alex Kiddell, Executive from Monex UK During the event, Nick will explore the key geopolitical and macroeconomic themes shaping the global business environment as we look towards 2027. Drawing on insights from Monex's research team, he will discuss potential market implications arising from fiscal policy developments
